problems.title: A remainder after substitution
problems.question: x=7n+3. Find the remainder of 3x−5 when divided by 7.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
steps: The first term is divisible by 7; the remainder is 4.

problems.title: Two one-third segments
problems.question: C lies inside AB; K lies on AC with AK=2KC; P lies on CB with PB=2CP. If KP=4m, find AB.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: KC=AC/3 and CP=CB/3.
steps: Thus KP=KC+CP=(AC+CB)/3=AB/3. Therefore AB=12m.

problems.title: Two successive angle bisectors
problems.question: BK bisects∠ABC and BD bisects∠KBC. If∠ABD=90°, find∠DBC.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: Let∠DBC=t. Then∠KBC=2t and∠ABC=4t.

problems.title: Apply a custom operation twice
problems.question: Define a■b=(3a−2b)/(a+b). Find(1■0)■1.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.

problems.title: Three symmetric differences
problems.question: A={1,2,3,4,5}, B={2,4,6,8}, C={0,3,6}. Find|(A△B)△C|.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: Symmetric difference retains elements in exactly one of the two sets.
steps: A△B={1,3,5,6,8}. Taking symmetric difference with C removes3,6 and adds0.
The final set is{0,1,5,8}, of size4.

problems.title: The forced common multiple
problems.question: A is divisible by 4,9,6,12,18. Which listed integer must divide A?
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
steps: A must be a multiple of 36. Taking A=36 also shows that none of 48,24,108,72,216 is forced.

problems.title: Two angle sizes at parallel lines
problems.question: A transversal cuts parallel lines. Two of the 8 angles sum 160°. Find the largest angle.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: The angle sizes areθ and 180°−θ. Different sizes would sum 180°, so the chosen two have equal size80°.
steps: The other size is 100°, which is larger.

problems.title: Subtract fractional positions
problems.question: C, D lie inside AB with AC:CB=2:5, AD:DB=6:11. If CD=8, find AB.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: AC=2AB/7, AD=6AB/17.

problems.title: Euclid’s subtraction rule
problems.question: Which listed gcd equality always holds for positive a>b?
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: gcd(a, b)=gcd(a−b, b).
steps: A number divides both a, b exactly when it divides both a−b, b. Multiplying just one argument can introduce extra common factors, so the other proposed identities are not universal.

problems.title: Exactly five divisors
problems.question: A positive integer n has exactly 5 positive divisors. What must its for m be?
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: If n=∏pᵢ^eᵢ, its divisor count is∏(eᵢ+1).
steps: Since 5 is prime, there is just one prime factor and its exponent is 4. Thus n=p⁴ for a prime p.

problems.title: An arithmetic mean of segment lengths
problems.question: A, C, D, B occur in order; AC:CD=2:3, DB=2.5, and AC is the mean of CD, DB. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: Write AC=2t, CD=3t. Then 2t=(3t+2.5)/2.
steps: This gives t=2.5. Therefore AB=5+7.5+2.5=15.

problems.title: Supplementary angles from fractional equality
problems.question: Two adjacent supplementary angles satisfy A/3=B/2. Find their difference.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
steps: They are 108°,72°; difference 36°.

problems.title: Keep the leading minus sign
problems.question: Evaluate −(−2)²·(−(−3·(−2−1)+3)+1).
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
steps: The parenthesis is −12+1=−11. The outside factor is −4, so the product is 44.

problems.title: Cycle of last digits
problems.question: Find the last digit of 2023²⁰²³.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: Powers of 3 have last-digit cycle3,9,7,1 of length 4.
steps: 2023 has remainder3 modulo4, so the final digit is 7.

problems.title: Segments within and across half-planes
problems.question: There are 3 points on one side of a line and 4 on the other. How many more cross-side segments than same-side segments?
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: Cross-side count=3·4=12; same-side count=C(3,2)+C(4,2)=3+6=9.
steps: The difference is 12−9=3.

problems.title: Use the direction of a ray
problems.question: B lies on ray OA with OB>OA; OA=15, AB=7. C lies on ray AO and CB=10. Find OC.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: Set O=0, A=15, B=22. Ray AO consists of coordinates≤15.
steps: Distance from B gives C=12 or 32. Only 12 lies on ray AO. Hence OC=12.

problems.title: Difference between nested-angle bisectors
problems.question: OC lies inside∠AOB. The bisectors of∠BOC and∠AOB make70°. Find∠AOC.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: Let∠AOB=T and∠AOC=u. Their bisector directions from OA are T/2 and(T+u)/2.
steps: Their difference is u/2=70°, so u=140°.

problems.title: Parallel lines and a right-angle turn
problems.question: In the diagram AF∥DC, AD bisects∠BAF,∠ADC=25°, and∠ABC=90°. Find∠BCD.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: Parallel-line angle relations give∠FAD=25°, so∠FAB=50°.
steps: AB therefore makes50° with the parallel lines. Since BC⊥AB, BC makes40° with them, so∠BCD=40°.

problems.title: Vertical angles repeat
problems.question: Three lines meet and form6 acute angles. Three are 50°,70°,60°. Find the largest of the other 3.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: The 6 angles occur in3 equal opposite pairs.
steps: The three distinct given sizes occupy one of each pair. The remaining angles are 50°,70°,60°, so their maximum is 70°.

problems.title: Same remainder means divisible differences
problems.question: x, y, z leave the same remainder modulo natural n>1. Given x−y=52, z−x=39, find n.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: n must divide both 52 and 39, so it divides gcd(52,39)=13.
steps: Since 13 is prime and n>1, the only possibility is n=13.

problems.title: Clock hands catch up
problems.question: At17:17, how long until the clock hands next coincide?
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: Minute-hand angle=17·6=102°. Hour-hand angle=5·30+17·0.5=158.5°. Relative speed=6−0.5=5.5°/min.

problems.title: First six-digit multiple
problems.question: Find the number formed by the first 4 digits of the least6-digit multiple of 396.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
steps: The least qualifying multiple is 100188, whose first 4 digits form1001.

problems.title: Express parts of a total
problems.question: The first number is half the sum of the other 2, the second is one third of the other 2, and the third is 30. Find their sum.
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: If the total is S, the first is S/3 and the second S/4.
steps: The third is S−S/3−S/4=5S/12=30, so S=72.

problems.title: Recover a set’s size
problems.question: A set has 32 subsets. How many elements does it have?
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: A set of n elements has 2ⁿ subsets.
steps: Since 32=2⁵, the set has 5 elements.

problems.title: Divisor counts of three prime cubes
problems.question: Multiply3 independently chosen prime cubes. How many different divisor counts can the product have?
problems.idea: Use the given ratios, angle relations, or divisibility facts directly.
formulas: The primes can all differ, exactly 2 can agree, or all 3 can agree.
steps: The exponent patterns are(3,3,3),(6,3),(9), giving divisor counts4³=64,7·4=28, and 10.
These are 3 distinct possible counts.
